FailList.Trigger: A valid grading capture is accepted, and the operator, who holds the unblinding map, computes an unfavorable aggregate before calling LockBlindGrades.
FailList.Problem: The attempt limits, the one-lock rule and 'No regrade follows a valid low score' all apply per Evaluation SubjectDigest, and that digest includes the results digests. Nothing makes a protocol's complete RecordResults packet final. A later complete packet with any byte change in resultJson creates a new subject with a fresh attempt 0, and that subject's lock satisfies the 'frozen protocol has a lock' check. AbandonProtocol also refuses only locked protocols, so a protocol with an accepted but unlocked grading can be abandoned. Activation never refuses on such a grading.
FailList.Consequence: A valid unfavorable blind grading can be discarded, either by re-recording results (leaving no abandonment record) or by abandoning the protocol (which records the abandonment but hides that a valid grading existed). This reopens the selective-grading path that §21.1 claims to close for the evaluation that gates activation.
FailList.RequiredResolution: Add to §21.1: (a) Per workspace and protocolId, once a grading attempt is allocated for a results subject, that complete RecordResults packet is final. A different later complete packet for the protocol is refused with 409 evaluation_results_locked; an identical repeat is idempotent. Before any attempt exists, a corrected packet may supersede it, with both retained in accounting. Accepted runs' EvalResult bytes become immutable once an attempt exists. (b) AbandonProtocol is refused once any grading attempt for that protocol holds an accepted capture; that grading must reach LockBlindGrades or GradingInvalid, and the failing-lock rule then applies. (c) Activation for a workspace/policy/build also refuses while any grading attempt holds an accepted capture without a lock. Tests: a differing packet after attempt allocation is refused; abandonment after an accepted capture is refused; an unlocked accepted capture blocks activation; correction before any attempt is allowed and disclosed.

## Finding
- **R12-01 (Medium): a valid low grading can still be thrown away.** The grading-attempt limits, the one-lock rule and 'no regrade after a valid low score' (§21.1) apply per Evaluation SubjectDigest, and that digest includes the results digests. Nothing makes a protocol's complete RecordResults packet final, so re-recording results with any byte change creates a fresh subject whose lock satisfies 'frozen protocol has a lock'. AbandonProtocol refuses only locked protocols, so a protocol with an accepted but unlocked grading can be abandoned. Activation never refuses on accepted gradings that were not locked. Because the operator holds the map, they can see an unfavorable result before locking and discard it.
- **Fix:** (a) once a grading attempt exists, the protocol's complete packet is final (409 evaluation_results_locked; identical repeat idempotent; corrections only before any attempt) and accepted EvalResult bytes are immutable; (b) refuse AbandonProtocol once a grading capture is accepted; (c) activation refuses while any accepted capture is unlocked. Add tests for each.
